text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
SABAH
- Dissidents in Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller's secularist wing of the coalition could block planned revamping of the government.
- Turkey asks for the extradition from the United States of Asil Nadir's former wife Aysegul, wanted in Turkey for smuggling antiquities.
MILLIYET
- Two assailants attacked Istanbul police headquarters with a light anti-tank rocket. The rocket hit the wall and caused little damage.
- The inflation rate under the Islamist-led government climbed to 80 percent and interest rates stood at 110 percent.
HURRIYET
- President Suleyman Demirel vetoed a draft law aiming to close down casinos in Turkey.
- The trade minister from the government's conservative wing has approved a military-inspired crackdwon on Islamist bussinesses.
YENI YUZYIL
- Today marks the first anniversary of the Islamist-conservative coalition government coming to power.
- The justice minister from the government's Islamist wing will re-appoint some 1,200 judges and prosecutors to distant posts for attending a military briefing on Islamic activism last week.
RADIKAL

- The plan for extending compulsory education to eight years demanded by the army among steps to clamp down on Islamist activism, has been shelved due to lack of time for it to be implemented before the next academic year.
CUMHURIYET
- Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan again blamed "certain sections of the media" for the tension between the government and the armed forces.
DUNYA
- Food producers not following the instructions of the health ministry will be shut by July 10.
- Turkey's Sabanci Holding and Germany's Hoechst have layed the foundations for a joint cord fabric factory in western Turkey.
ZAMAN
- Rumours of poltical tension over the last three months have cost the country billions of dollars in foreign investment.
